title: Relayer Multisig signers are self-administered while Freezer Multisig signers can only change by Atlas Edit Proposal
content:
The two privileged multisigs in the Pattern Liquidity Layer have deliberately different amendment rules.

For the Relayer Multisig, A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5 says "Operational GovOps Soter Labs can change the signers... **at any time**, so long as there are at least three (3) signers and at least two-thirds of signers are required to execute transactions." Authority is delegated wholesale, constrained only by two structural floors — a minimum signer count and a minimum threshold ratio — rather than by approval of any particular signer set.

For the Freezer Multisig, A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.2.5 says "Modification of the signers... **must be approved through an Atlas Edit Proposal**," with only two narrow exceptions: a signer self-reporting lost key access, or a signer asking to be removed — each requiring a public Sky Forum post.

The distinction tracks what each key can do. Relayer keys operate the system inside limits that admin sets and rate limits enforce, so rotating them is routine operational hygiene and demanding a governance vote for each change would create dangerous delay. Freezer keys are the check *on* the operator, so allowing the operator's employer to reshuffle them would let the supervised party choose its supervisors.

The two exceptions are carefully shaped to preserve that logic: both are ways for a signer to *reduce* their own participation, which cannot be used to pack the multisig.
description: Soter Labs may rotate Relayer signers at will subject to a three-signer, two-thirds floor; changing who holds the emergency brake requires ecosystem governance approval instead.
